stem: The distance moved by an object in a unit of time is its __________.
solution: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time.

stem: The SI unit of speed is __________.
solution: The SI unit of speed is metre per second (m/s).

stem: Speed is calculated using the formula __________.
solution: Speed = total distance travelled ÷ total time taken.

stem: A car travels 150 km in 3 hours. Its speed is __________.
solution: Speed = 150 km ÷ 3 h = 50 km/h.

stem: An object that covers equal distances in equal intervals of time is in __________.
solution: In uniform motion, an object covers equal distances in equal time intervals (constant speed).

stem: An object that covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time is in __________.
solution: Non-uniform motion means the speed changes, covering unequal distances in equal times.

stem: The SI unit of time is the __________.
solution: The SI unit of time is the second (s).

stem: Ancient people measured time using periodic natural events like __________.
options: day and night and phases of the Moon
solution: Periodic events like day/night and lunar phases were used to measure time.

stem: A device that measures time using the regular swings of a pendulum is a __________.
solution: A pendulum clock uses the regular oscillations of a pendulum to keep time.

stem: The to-and-fro motion of a pendulum is an example of __________ motion.
solution: A pendulum repeats its swing at regular intervals — periodic (oscillatory) motion.

stem: The time taken by a pendulum to complete one full oscillation is called its __________.
solution: The time period is the time for one complete oscillation of the pendulum.

stem: The time period of a simple pendulum depends mainly on its __________.
solution: The time period of a simple pendulum depends on its length.

stem: 1 hour is equal to __________ seconds.
solution: 1 hour = 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds.

stem: The instrument that shows the speed of a vehicle is the __________.
solution: A speedometer indicates the speed of a vehicle.

stem: The instrument that records the total distance travelled by a vehicle is the __________.
solution: The odometer records the total distance covered by a vehicle.

stem: On a distance–time graph, uniform motion is shown by a __________.
solution: Uniform motion (constant speed) gives a straight, sloping line on a distance–time graph.

stem: On a distance–time graph, an object at rest is shown by a __________.
solution: An object at rest keeps the same position, giving a horizontal line.

stem: On a distance–time graph, a steeper slope indicates __________.
solution: A steeper line means more distance per unit time, i.e., a greater speed.

stem: A train covers 300 km in 5 hours. Its average speed is __________.
solution: Speed = 300 km ÷ 5 h = 60 km/h.

stem: The average speed of an object is found by dividing the __________.
options: total distance by the total time
solution: Average speed = total distance travelled ÷ total time taken.

stem: A sundial measures time using the __________.
options: position of the shadow cast by the Sun
solution: A sundial uses the moving shadow of the Sun to indicate the time of day.

stem: The device used to measure very small time intervals, as in races, is a __________.
solution: A stopwatch measures short time intervals precisely.

stem: Modern clocks often keep accurate time using the vibrations of a __________ crystal.
solution: Quartz clocks use the regular vibrations of a quartz crystal to keep time.

stem: 1 kilometre is equal to __________ metres.
The larger unit of speed used for vehicles on roads is usually __________.
solution: Vehicle speeds are conveniently expressed in kilometres per hour (km/h).

stem: A body moving in a straight line with changing speed is in __________.
solution: Changing speed along a straight line is non-uniform (straight-line) motion.

stem: The speed of a moving object tells us __________.
options: how fast or slow it is moving
solution: Speed indicates how fast an object is moving.

stem: 72 km/h expressed in m/s is __________.
To convert km/h into m/s, multiply by __________.
solution: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s, so multiply km/h by 5/18 to get m/s.

stem: If a pendulum's time period is 2 seconds, then in 1 minute it makes __________ oscillations.
solution: 60 s ÷ 2 s per oscillation = 30 oscillations per minute.

stem: A pendulum with a longer thread will have a __________ time period.
solution: A longer pendulum swings more slowly, so its time period is greater.

stem: On a distance–time graph, time is usually plotted along the __________.
solution: Time is plotted on the horizontal x-axis and distance on the vertical y-axis.

stem: A water clock measures time by the __________.
options: steady dripping or flow of water
solution: A water clock (clepsydra) measures time by the steady flow of water.

stem: A sand clock (hourglass) measures a fixed time interval using the __________.
options: steady flow of sand between two bulbs
solution: An hourglass measures a fixed time by the steady flow of sand from one bulb to another.

stem: An object taking a shorter time to cover a given distance has a __________ speed.
solution: For the same distance, less time taken means a higher speed.

stem: The scientist whose study of the pendulum led to pendulum clocks was __________.
solution: Galileo studied the regular period of a swinging pendulum, which later led to pendulum clocks.

stem: A cyclist rides 12 km in 30 minutes. The average speed is __________.
solution: 30 min = 0.5 h; speed = 12 km ÷ 0.5 h = 24 km/h.

stem: A vehicle moving at a steady 40 km/h on a straight road shows __________.
solution: A steady 40 km/h is uniform motion — equal distances in equal times.

stem: The maximum displacement of a pendulum bob from its central position is its __________.
solution: Amplitude is the maximum distance the bob moves from its mean (central) position.

stem: Which of the following is used to measure the distance between two cities?
solution: Large distances like those between cities are expressed in kilometres.

stem: Standard units of time and distance are used so that measurements are __________.
solution: Standard units ensure consistent and comparable measurements worldwide.

stem: If a bus covers 30 km in the first hour and 50 km in the second, its motion is __________.
solution: Different distances in equal time intervals mean the motion is non-uniform.

stem: A larger unit of time than the second includes the __________.
solution: Minute, hour and day are larger units of time than the second.

stem: The unit 'm/s' for speed is derived from the units of __________.
solution: Speed is distance/time, so its unit combines metre and second.

stem: A body at rest on a distance–time graph shows __________.
options: no change in distance with time
solution: At rest, distance stays constant with time — a horizontal line.

stem: The reading of the odometer of a car increases as the car __________.
solution: The odometer records total distance travelled, so it increases as the car covers more distance.

stem: Which of the following is the correct increasing order of length units?
A vehicle moving at 90 km/h in m/s is __________.
The main idea of measuring motion is to describe __________.
options: how the position of an object changes with time
solution: Describing motion means tracking how an object's position changes over time.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Measurement of Time and Motion' is that:
options: motion is described using speed (distance per unit time), and time is measured using periodic events like the swing of a pendulum, represented by distance–time graphs
solution: The chapter links motion to speed and shows how periodic motion measures time, using distance–time graphs.
